source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. V (Montreuil)

1.title: Expositio capituli primi: In anno primo Cyri regis Persarum
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians

paras.t: Exordium libri hujus cum fine secundi Paralipomenon libri coincidit, ut intuentibus constat. Unde et Esdras editor libri istius, illius quoque libri creditur auctor. Itaque ait: In anno primo Cyri regis Persarum. Quod non est intelligendum de primo anno vitæ Cyri istius, neque de primo anno simplicis et particularis regni ejus, sed de primo anno regni ejus imperialis monarchici. Quum enim una cum Dario suo avunculo destruxisset monarchiam Chaldæorum, et eorum metropolim Babylonem urbem evertisset, Darius tenuit monarchiam annis duobus. Quo mortuo, Cyrus monarcha effectus, primo suæ monarchiæ anno dedit Judæis a Nabuchodonosor rege Babyloniæ transmigratis et captis, licentiam redeundi ad propria, sicut subjungitur. Ut compleretur verbum Domini prolatum ex ore Jeremiæ, suscitavit Dominus spiritum Cyri regis Persarum, hoc est, mentem ejus instigavit inspiratione occulta, interna, et etiam per quædam exteriora, sicut tangetur. Et transduxit vocem, id est, denuntiationem fecit per scripta et nuntios, in omni regno suo, id est per totam suam monarchiam: hinc subditur, etiam per scripturam, id est epistolas, dicens.
paras.en: The opening of this book coincides with the end of the second book of Paralipomenon, as is plain to those who look[[2 Par 36:22||]][[2 Par 36:23||]]. Hence Esdras, the writer of this book, is believed to be the author of that book also. And so he says: [[1:1|In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians|In anno primo Cyri regis Persarum]]. This is not to be understood of the first year of this Cyrus's life, nor of the first year of his plain and particular kingship, but of the first year of his imperial reign as monarch. For when, together with Darius his uncle, he had destroyed the monarchy of the Chaldeans and overthrown their capital, the city of Babylon, Darius held the monarchy for two years. On his death Cyrus became monarch, and in the first year of his monarchy he gave the Jews, who had been carried away and taken captive by Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon[[4 Kings 25:11||]][[4 Kings 25:21||]], leave to return to their own land[[2 Par 36:22||]], as follows: [[1:1|that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias might be fulfilled|Ut compleretur verbum Domini prolatum ex ore Jeremiæ]], [[1:1|the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians|suscitavit Dominus spiritum Cyri regis Persarum]], that is, He urged on his mind by a hidden, inward inspiration, and also through certain outward things, as will be touched on. [[1:1|and he made a proclamation|Et transduxit vocem]], that is, he made it known by writings and messengers, [[1:1|throughout all his kingdom|in omni regno suo]], that is, through his whole monarchy: hence it is added, [[1:1|and in writing also|etiam per scripturam]], that is, by letters, [[1:1|saying|dicens]].

paras.t: Prædixerat autem Dominus in Jeremia: Quum cœperint impleri in Babylone septuaginta anni, id est, septuaginta annis completis a tempore transmigrationis seu captivitatis Judæorum a Chaldæis, visitabo vos et suscitabo super vos verbum meum bonum, ut reducam vos ad locum istum. De quibus annis fit mentio apud Zachariam et Danielem, quamvis computatio annorum illorum a diversis diversimode assignetur, sicut in Scholastica historia satis habetur. Erantque anni illi impleti, Cyro monarcha effecto. Ideo Dominus volens verba et promissa sua per Jeremiam prænuntiata implere, excitavit et movit cor Cyri ad dandum præfatam redeundi licentiam. Ad quod etiam fuit inductus, quia Judæi captivi ostenderunt sibi librum Isaiæ prophetæ, et quadragesimum quintum capitulum libri ejusdem, in quo et nomen ipsius Cyri fuit tam diu ante expressum, et reædificatio civitatis Jerusalem de Cyri licentia fienda, clarissime prophetata his verbis: Hæc dicit Dominus christo meo Cyro, cujus apprehendi dexteram, ut subjiciam ante faciem ejus gentes et dorsa regum vertam; ipse ædificabit civitatem meam. Porro de templi reædificatione non in capitulo isto, sed immediate præcedente, Dominus prædixit per Isaiam: Qui dico Cyro, Pastor meus es; et templo, Ædificaberis. Hæc autem per annos ducentos et decem per Isaiam fuerunt prædicta, ut Josephus scribit.
paras.en: Now the Lord had foretold in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:10|When the seventy years shall begin to be accomplished in Babylon|Quum cœperint impleri in Babylone septuaginta anni]], that is, when seventy years are completed from the time of the carrying away or captivity of the Jews by the Chaldeans, [[Jer 29:10|I will visit you: and I will perform my good word in your favour, to bring you again to this place|visitabo vos et suscitabo super vos verbum meum bonum, ut reducam vos ad locum istum]]. Of these years mention is made in Zacharias[[Zach 1:12||]] and Daniel[[Dan 9:2||]], though the reckoning of those years is assigned in different ways by different writers, as is set out at length in the Scholastic History. And those years were fulfilled when Cyrus became monarch. Therefore the Lord, willing to fulfil His words and promises foretold by Jeremias, roused and moved the heart of Cyrus to give the aforesaid leave to return. He was led to this also because the captive Jews showed him the book of the prophet Isaias, and the forty-fifth chapter of that book, in which the name of Cyrus himself was set down so long before, and the rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem by the leave of Cyrus was most clearly prophesied in these words: [[Is 45:1|Thus saith the Lord to my anointed Cyrus, whose right hand I have taken hold of, to subdue nations before his face, and to turn the backs of kings|Hæc dicit Dominus christo meo Cyro, cujus apprehendi dexteram, ut subjiciam ante faciem ejus gentes et dorsa regum vertam]]; [[Is 45:13|he shall build my city|ipse ædificabit civitatem meam]]. As for the rebuilding of the temple, the Lord foretold it by Isaias not in that chapter but in the one immediately before: [[Is 44:28|Who say to Cyrus: Thou art my shepherd|Qui dico Cyro, Pastor meus es]]; [[Is 44:28|and to the temple|et templo]], [[Is 44:28|Thou shalt be built|Ædificaberis]] [in Isaias these words are said to Jerusalem; to the temple he says *Fundaberis*, “Thy foundations shall be laid”]. These things were foretold by Isaias two hundred and ten years before, as Josephus writes.

paras.t: Hoc dicit Cyrus rex Persarum. Sicut Magister in historiis recolit, post mortem Darii regis Medorum, Cyrus monarchiam tenuit orientis. Eratque rex Persarum atque Medorum, quia Darius ille non habuit filium; et quamvis regnum Medorum fuerat majus ac honorabilius regno Persarum, Cyrus tamen posuit solium monarchiæ in Perside, quoniam Persæ sublimaverant eum primo in regem. Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Dominus Deus cæli: cujus providentiæ cuncta subduntur terrena. Hoc tamen per hyperbolen dictum est, ad insinuandum quod valde magna regna erant ei subjecta in oriente; non tamen simpliciter omnia regna terræ, imo nec absolute omnia regna orientis. Et ipse præcepit mihi per inspirationem internam, et per Prophetam suum prænuntiavit, ut ædificarem ei domum, id est templum, in Jerusalem, id est in loco ubi ante sita fuit Jerusalem, et ubi jam rursus construetur ex mea licentia, quæ est quantum ad fundum suum, et cito erit, in Judæa.
paras.en: [[1:2|Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians|Hoc dicit Cyrus rex Persarum]]. As the Master recalls in the Histories [Peter Comestor, *Historia scholastica*], after the death of Darius king of the Medes, Cyrus held the monarchy of the East. And he was king of the Persians and of the Medes, because that Darius had no son; and though the kingdom of the Medes was greater and more honourable than the kingdom of the Persians, Cyrus nevertheless set the throne of the monarchy in Persia, since the Persians had first raised him to be king. [[1:2|The Lord the God of heaven hath given to me all the kingdoms of the earth|Omnia regna terræ dedit mihi Dominus Deus cæli]], to whose providence all earthly things are subject. Yet this was said by hyperbole, to convey that very great kingdoms in the East were subject to him; but not simply all the kingdoms of the earth, nor indeed absolutely all the kingdoms of the East. [[1:2|and he hath charged me|Et ipse præcepit mihi]] by an inward inspiration, and foretold it by His Prophet, [[1:2|to build him a house|ut ædificarem ei domum]], that is, a temple, [[1:2|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], that is, in the place where Jerusalem formerly stood, and where it will now be built again by my leave, [[1:2|which is|quæ est]] as to its ground, and soon will be, [[1:2|in Judea|in Judæa]].

paras.t: Quis est in vobis, id est inter vos, de universo populo ejus, id est ex numero Judæorum? Sit Deus illius cum eo, per adsistentiam gratiosam. Ascendat in Jerusalem, id est ad locum quo stetit, et ædificet domum Dei Israel: id est, quicumque natus est ex populo Israel, ostendat se esse cultorem Dei cæli, ascendendo ad Judæam, ad reædificandum templum. Nec solum dedit licentiam ædificandi templum, sed et ipsam urbem Jerusalem: quam cœperunt reædificare antequam templum. Hanc autem gratuitam relaxationem captivitatis Judæorum Deus per Isaiam prædixit his verbis: Ipse captivitatem meam dimittet, non in pretio, neque in muneribus. Ipse est Deus qui est in Jerusalem, id est, Deus cæli urbem Jerusalem elegit in locum præcipuum cultus sui, et templi, ac sacrificiorum, et ita quamvis incircumscriptus sit, et præsens ubique, ibi tamen est per speciales effectus.
paras.en: [[1:3|Who is there among you|Quis est in vobis]], that is, between you, [[1:3|of all his people|de universo populo ejus]], that is, of the number of the Jews? [[1:3|His God be with him|Sit Deus illius cum eo]] by His gracious assistance. [[1:3|Let him go up to Jerusalem|Ascendat in Jerusalem]], that is, to the place where it stood, [[1:3|and build the house of the Lord the God of Israel|et ædificet domum Dei Israel]]: that is, whoever is born of the people of Israel, let him show himself a worshipper of the God of heaven by going up to Judæa to rebuild the temple. And he gave leave to build not only the temple but the city of Jerusalem itself, which they began to rebuild before the temple[[1 Esd 4:13||]] [the margin's reference is damaged; 1 Esdras iv tells of the rebuilding of the city]. This free release of the Jews from captivity God foretold by Isaias in these words: He shall [[Is 45:13|let go my captives, not for ransom, nor for presents|captivitatem meam dimittet, non in pretio, neque in muneribus]]. [[1:3|he is the God that is in Jerusalem|Ipse est Deus qui est in Jerusalem]]: that is, the God of heaven chose the city of Jerusalem[[2 Par 6:6||]] as the principal place of His worship, of the temple and of the sacrifices; and so, though He is uncircumscribed and present everywhere, yet He is there by special effects.

paras.t: Et omnes reliqui in cunctis locis ubicumque habitant, id est Judæi qui vel nolunt, aut nequeunt ad Judæam reverti, adjuvent eum, id est eos qui ascendunt illuc, viri de loco suo, id est, residui illi hoc faciant ex locis habitationum suarum in imperio meo, argento et auro, et substantia, et pecoribus, id est, dando eis in subsidium expensarum in via, vel reædificationis templi et urbis Jerusalem, aliquid de suo argento et auro, ac ceteris facultatibus ac jumentis, excepto quod voluntarie offerunt in templo Dei, quod est in Jerusalem, id est præter dona quæ ex propria devotione voluerint ad templi reædificationem sive ad sacrificia Dei ibi fienda offerre. Insuper quod dictum est, Et omnes reliqui adjuvent eum, potest intelligi de gentilibus inter quos habitabant Judæi: quibus gentilibus Cyrus jussit, ut Judæos in hac causa juvarent. Nam Josephus ait: Tunc scripsit suis ducibus illius terræ vicinis, ut aurum conferrent et argentum ad templi renovationem, insuper ad immolanda pecora. Refert quoque Josephus Cyrum ita scripsisse: Quoniam maximus Deus orbis terrarum me regem constituit, credo hunc esse quem gens Israel adorat. Is enim et nomen meum per Prophetas prædixit, quoniam templum ejus ædificaturus essem in Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:4|And let all the rest in all places wheresoever they dwell|Et omnes reliqui in cunctis locis ubicumque habitant]], that is, the Jews who either will not or cannot return to Judæa, [[1:4|help him|adjuvent eum]], that is, those who go up there, [[1:4|every man from his place|viri de loco suo]]: that is, let those who stay behind do this from the places where they dwell in my empire, [[1:4|with silver and gold, and goods, and cattle|argento et auro, et substantia, et pecoribus]]: that is, by giving them, as a help towards their expenses on the way or towards the rebuilding of the temple and the city of Jerusalem, something of their silver and gold and other means, and of their beasts; [[1:4|besides that which they offer freely to the temple of God, which is in Jerusalem|excepto quod voluntarie offerunt in templo Dei, quod est in Jerusalem]], that is, beyond the gifts which out of their own devotion they may wish to offer for the rebuilding of the temple or for the sacrifices of God to be made there. Moreover, what is said, *And let all the rest help him*, can be understood of the gentiles among whom the Jews were living: these gentiles Cyrus ordered to help the Jews in this matter. For Josephus says: “Then he wrote to his governors who were neighbours of that land, that they should contribute gold and silver for the renewing of the temple, and besides, cattle for sacrifice.” Josephus also relates that Cyrus wrote thus: “Since the most great God has made me king of the world, I believe that He is the one whom the nation of Israel adores. For He also foretold my name by the Prophets, that I should build His temple in Jerusalem.”

paras.t: Et surrexerunt omnes principes patrum, id est præcipui patres et majores seniorum, de Juda et Benjamin, et sacerdotes et Levitæ, id est qui nati fuerunt ex tribu Juda, tribuque Benjamin, atque ex tribu Levi. Hæ etenim tribus erant et manserant sub regibus Juda, diviso regno Israelitico sub Roboam filio Salomonis, et pariter captæ fuerunt. De hoc Josephus scribit: Convocans Cyrus clarissimos Judæorum qui in Babylone, id est in terra Babyloniæ, habitabant, dixit se concedere Judæos remeare ad propria, et reædificare civitatem Jerusalem et templum. Et omnis cujus suscitavit Deus spiritum, ut ascenderet ad ædificandum templum Domini, quod est in Jerusalem, id est quilibet de præfatis tribus tribubus Israel, cujus mentem Deus instigavit, ut ascenderet ad ædificandum templum.
paras.en: [[1:5|Then rose up the chief of the fathers|Et surrexerunt omnes principes patrum]], that is, the chief fathers and the elders among the old men, [[1:5|of Juda and Benjamin, and the priests, and Levites|de Juda et Benjamin, et sacerdotes et Levitæ]], that is, those born of the tribe of Juda, the tribe of Benjamin, and the tribe of Levi. For these tribes were and had remained under the kings of Juda when the kingdom of Israel was divided under Roboam the son of Solomon[[3 Kings 12:21||]][[2 Par 11:1||]][[2 Par 11:13||]], and they were taken captive together. Of this Josephus writes: “Cyrus, calling together the most distinguished of the Jews who dwelt in Babylon” (that is, in the land of Babylonia), “said that he granted the Jews to return to their own land, and to rebuild the city of Jerusalem and the temple.” [[1:5|and every one whose spirit God had raised up, to go up to build the temple of the Lord, which was in Jerusalem|Et omnis cujus suscitavit Deus spiritum, ut ascenderet ad ædificandum templum Domini, quod est in Jerusalem]]: that is, any one of the three aforesaid tribes of Israel whose mind God urged to go up to build the temple.

paras.t: Universique qui erant in circuitu Judæ, vel in circuitu Judæorum pergentium illuc, adjuverunt manus eorum in vasis argenteis et aureis, in substantia victualium, et jumentis et supellectili, id est massaritio: hoc est, talia clenodia et subsidia illis præstando. Quod quidam exponunt de Judæis in Babylonia remanentibus amore uxorum quas ibi acceperant, et sobolis quam ibi procreaverant, ac possessionum quas ibi habebant. Quidam vero exponunt, dicentes, quod gentiles de mandato Cyri talia dederunt Judæis pergentibus. Josephus quoque ait, quod dum Judæi venissent, omnes amici regis juvabant eos, et conferebant ad templi renovationem, alii aurum, alii argentum, alii equos et multitudinem jumentorum.
paras.en: [[1:6|And all they that were round about|Universique qui erant in circuitu]] Juda, or round about the Jews who were going there, [[1:6|helped their hands|adjuverunt manus eorum]] [[1:6|with vessels of silver, and gold|in vasis argenteis et aureis]], [[1:6|with goods|in substantia]] of victuals, [[1:6|and with beasts, and with furniture|et jumentis et supellectili]], that is, household goods: that is, by furnishing them with such valuables [*clenodia*, a late Latin word for treasures or precious things] and aids. Some explain this of the Jews who stayed in Babylonia for love of the wives they had taken there, and the children they had begotten there, and the possessions they had there. Others explain it by saying that the gentiles, at Cyrus's command, gave such things to the Jews as they went. Josephus too says that when the Jews had come, all the king's friends helped them and contributed to the renewing of the temple, some gold, some silver, some horses and a multitude of beasts.

paras.t: Rex quoque Cyrus protulit, hoc est exhibuit, vasa templi Domini, quæ fuerunt instrumenta et utensilia cultus divini in templo a Salomone constructo, quæ tulerat Nabuchodonosor de Jerusalem, id est ex templo inibi sito. Asportavit autem ea secum, partim quando captivavit Joakin regem, et partim dum Jechoniam abduxit, reliqua dum templum combussit, prout secundo Paralipomenon, ultimo, et quarto Regum libris describitur. Et posuerat ea in templo dei sui in urbe Babylonis: et sic juxta suam sectam ea quodammodo honoravit, ponendo ea in loco solenni et sacro, deputandoque ea cultui secundum suam æstimationem divino. Balthasar vero filius filii ejus deputavit ea cultui suo, bibendo ex eis cum suis, ut habetur in Daniele: propter quod meruit regno privari ac vita. Et aliqui opinantur quod Judæi retulerunt hoc Cyro: idcirco libentius ea remisit.
paras.en: [[1:7|And king Cyrus brought forth|Rex quoque Cyrus protulit]], that is, produced, [[1:7|vessels of the temple of the Lord|vasa templi Domini]], which were the instruments and utensils of the divine worship in the temple built by Solomon, [[1:7|which Nabuchodonosor had taken from Jerusalem|quæ tulerat Nabuchodonosor de Jerusalem]], that is, from the temple that stood there. He carried them off with him, partly when he took king Joakin captive[[2 Par 36:7||]], and partly when he led away Jechonias[[2 Par 36:10||]][[4 Kings 24:13||]], and the rest when he burned the temple[[2 Par 36:18||]][[4 Kings 25:13||]], as is described in the second book of Paralipomenon, the last chapter, and in the fourth book of Kings. [[1:7|and had put them in the temple of his god|Et posuerat ea in templo dei sui]] in the city of Babylon: and so, after the manner of his sect, he in a way honoured them, by putting them in a solemn and sacred place and setting them apart for what he reckoned divine worship. But Baltasar, his son's son, put them to his own use, drinking from them with his company, as we have it in Daniel[[Dan 5:2||]][[Dan 5:3||]]: for which he deserved to be deprived of his kingdom and his life. And some think that the Jews told this to Cyrus, and that he sent the vessels back the more willingly for it.

paras.t: Protulit autem ea Cyrus rex per manum Mithridatis, qui secundum Josephum fuit custos thesaurorum ipsius, et annumeravit ea Sassabasar principi Juda: hoc est, thesaurarius ille sub certo numero assignavit et tradidit vasa illa viro nomine Sassabasar principi Juda, id est uni de principalibus tribus seu populi Juda, seu duci redeuntium ad Judæam. Dicuntque aliqui, quod Sassabasar ille fuit Daniel; alii, quod fuit Zorobabel: quod magis consonum videtur ei quod in fine hujus capituli legitur: Universa tulit Sassabasar, cum his qui ascendebant de transmigratione Babylonis in Jerusalem. Daniel quippe cum illis non rediit, sed Zorobabel.
paras.en: [[1:8|Now Cyrus king of Persia brought them forth|Protulit autem ea Cyrus rex]] [[1:8|by the hand of Mithridates|per manum Mithridatis]], who according to Josephus was the keeper of his treasures, [[1:8|and numbered them to Sassabasar the prince of Juda|et annumeravit ea Sassabasar principi Juda]]: that is, that treasurer assigned and handed over those vessels, by a fixed count, to a man named Sassabasar, a prince of Juda, that is, to one of the chief men of the tribe or people of Juda, or to the leader of those returning to Judæa. And some say that this Sassabasar was Daniel; others that he was Zorobabel, which seems more in keeping with what we read at the end of this chapter: [[1:11|all these Sassabasar brought with them that came up from the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem|Universa tulit Sassabasar, cum his qui ascendebant de transmigratione Babylonis in Jerusalem]]. For Daniel did not return with them, but Zorobabel did.

paras.t: Et hic est numerus eorum: Phialæ aureæ triginta, phialæ argenteæ mille. Phialæ erant vasa, in quibus vinum libationis fusum considerabatur, an esset aptum ad sacrificia. Cultelli, quibus carnes hostiarum dividebantur, viginti novem; scyphi aurei triginta, scyphi argentei secundi, id est inferioris dignitatis, valoris et usus, quadringenti decem; vasa alia mille. In scyphis recipiebatur sanguis hostiarum, præsertim in scyphis argenteis. In aureis vero scyphis (ut fertur) portabatur sanguis sacrificiorum quorumdam intra Sancta sanctorum in festo Expiationis. Omnia vasa aurea et argentea, quinque millia quadringenta. Universa tulit Sassabasar, cum his qui ascendebant de transmigratione Babylonis in Jerusalem. Certum quod numerus prædictorum vasorum jam numeratorum, non constituit tantam summam; sed præter illa fuerunt alia multa minus forsitan pretiosa: quæ omnia simul fuerunt tot millia ac centenaria.
paras.en: [[1:9|And this is the number of them|Et hic est numerus eorum]]: [[1:9|thirty bowls of gold|Phialæ aureæ triginta]], [[1:9|a thousand bowls of silver|phialæ argenteæ mille]]. The bowls were vessels in which the wine of the libation was poured and examined, whether it were fit for the sacrifices[[Ex 25:29||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxv; the bowls for libations are at v. 29]. [[1:9|nine and twenty knives|Cultelli, quibus carnes hostiarum dividebantur, viginti novem]], with which the flesh of the victims was divided; [[1:9|thirty cups of gold|scyphi aurei triginta]], [[1:10|Silver cups of a second sort|scyphi argentei secundi]], that is, of lower dignity, value and use, [[1:10|four hundred and ten|quadringenti decem]]; [[1:10|other vessels a thousand|vasa alia mille]]. In the cups the blood of the victims was received, above all in the silver cups; but in the golden cups (so it is said) the blood of certain sacrifices was carried into the Holy of holies on the feast of the Expiation. [[1:11|All the vessels of gold and silver, five thousand four hundred|Omnia vasa aurea et argentea, quinque millia quadringenta]]. [[1:11|all these Sassabasar brought with them that came up from the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem|Universa tulit Sassabasar, cum his qui ascendebant de transmigratione Babylonis in Jerusalem]]. It is certain that the number of the vessels already counted does not make so great a sum [the vessels listed come to 2,499]; but besides them there were many others, perhaps less precious, all of which together made up so many thousands and hundreds.

paras.t: Postremo, de Cyro isto rege Persarum multa in Josepho et Scholastica historia, chronicisque leguntur: qui et triginta annis fertur regnasse, ac monarchiam annis duodecim tenuisse. Qui quum grandiusculus esset, et a pueris ludentibus esset factus eorum rex, inobedientes pueros dire correxit et interdum plagavit. Quod puerorum parentes ægre ferentes, conquesti sunt regi Astyagi avo Cyri, qui jusserat puerum ipsum mox natum occidi; sed Deo ordinante fuit conservatus in vita. Quumque rex puerum Cyrum ad se vocatum argueret, cur pueros ita plagasset, respondit intrepide se hoc fecisse, non ut puerum, sed ut regem: quo audito, miratus est rex, et signa quædam generis sui consideravit in eo. Tandem quum Cyrus monarcha reges plurimos expugnasset, a regina Massagetarum nomine Thamsyri victus est et occisus: quæ caput ipsius Cyri abscisum, projecit in vas humano sanguine plenum, dicens cum insultatione: Satiare nunc sanguine quem semper sitisti.
paras.en: Lastly, many things are read of this Cyrus king of the Persians in Josephus, in the Scholastic History and in the chronicles. He is said to have reigned thirty years and to have held the monarchy twelve years. When he was a growing boy, and had been made king by the boys at play, he corrected the disobedient boys severely and sometimes beat them. The boys' parents took this ill and complained to king Astyages, Cyrus's grandfather, who had ordered that the child be killed as soon as he was born; but by God's ordering he had been kept alive. And when the king called the boy Cyrus to him and reproved him for beating the boys so, he answered fearlessly that he had done it not as a boy but as a king: hearing which the king wondered, and saw in him certain signs of his own stock. At length, when Cyrus as monarch had conquered a great many kings, he was defeated and slain by the queen of the Massagetae, named Thamsyris, who threw Cyrus's severed head into a vessel full of human blood, saying in mockery: “Glut thyself now with the blood thou hast always thirsted for.”

paras.t: Circa illud, Surrexerunt principes patrum de Juda, ait quidam, quod tribus Juda et Benjamin et Levi, non tantum peccaverunt sicut aliæ tribus Israel per Assyrios captæ. Sed hoc non videtur consonare Scripturis, quoniam per Ezechielem Dominus ait ad Jerusalem, per quam, secundum omnes expositores, ad litteram intelligit populum regni Juda, et præsertim habitatores Jerusalem: Samaria dimidium peccatorum tuorum non peccavit; sed vicisti eas, scilicet Sodomam et Samariam, sceleribus tuis: et certum est, quod per Samariam intelligat regnum decem tribuum, cujus Samaria fuit metropolis. Idem patet in Ezechiele sub similitudine Oollæ et Oolibæ.
paras.en: On the words [[1:5|Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Juda|Surrexerunt principes patrum de Juda]], someone says that the tribes of Juda, Benjamin and Levi did not sin as much as the other tribes of Israel, which were taken captive by the Assyrians. But this does not seem to agree with the Scriptures, since by Ezechiel the Lord says to Jerusalem, by which, according to all the expositors, He means literally the people of the kingdom of Juda, and above all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: [[Ezech 16:51|And Samaria committed not half thy sins|Samaria dimidium peccatorum tuorum non peccavit]]: [[Ezech 16:51|but thou hast surpassed them|sed vicisti eas]], namely Sodom and Samaria, [[Ezech 16:51|with thy crimes|sceleribus tuis]]. And it is certain that by Samaria He means the kingdom of the ten tribes, whose capital Samaria was. The same is plain in Ezechiel under the figure of Oolla and Ooliba[[Ezech 23:4||]].

paras.t: At vero potest hoc loco per Cyrum allegorice Dominus Jesus Christus verus mundi monarcha intelligi: qui destructo regno diaboli, ædificavit per servos suos Ecclesiam; et fassus est se omne quod habet et est, accepisse a Patre: quod per Scripturas Evangelistarum universo orbi notificavit; et vasa Dei abducta reduxit, electos, qui a diabolo erant seducti, vitiorumque vinculis irretiti, reducendo ad gratiam ac salutem.
paras.en: But in this place Cyrus can be understood allegorically as the Lord Jesus Christ, the true monarch of the world, who, having destroyed the kingdom of the devil, built the Church through His servants; and He confessed that all He has and is He received from the Father[[John 5:26||]] [the margin gives John v, passim], which He made known to the whole world through the writings of the Evangelists; and He brought back the vessels of God that had been carried off, by bringing back to grace and salvation the elect, who had been led astray by the devil and entangled in the bonds of vice.

2.title: Expositio capituli secundi: Hi sunt autem provinciæ filii, qui ascenderunt de captivitate
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: Now these are the children of the province, that went out of the captivity

paras.t: Hic particularius describuntur reversi de Babylone.
paras.en: Here those who returned from Babylon are described in more detail.

paras.t: Hi sunt autem provinciæ filii, hoc est habitatores Babyloniæ, vel, ut quidam dicunt, Judæ. Porro nati et commorati in territorio aliquo, appellantur filii ejus. Qui ascenderunt de captivitate, id est de terra captivitatis suæ, puta de Babylonia, quam, hoc est cujus captivitatis plebem, vel, quam plebem captivam, transtulerat Nabuchodonosor in Babylonem, et reversi sunt in Jerusalem, et in Judam: unusquisque in civitatem suam, id est ad loca in quibus antea steterant urbs Jerusalem et alia oppida regni Juda a Chaldæis destructa. Quemadmodum enim aves diligunt suos nidos, et bruta sua latibula, sic homines sua loca nativa. Unde Laban ait ad Jacob: Ad tuos ire cupiebas, et desiderio tibi fuit domus patris tui. Hinc hortatur Apostolus: Non deserentes collectionem nostram.
paras.en: [[2:1|Now these are the children of the province|Hi sunt autem provinciæ filii]], that is, the inhabitants of Babylonia, or, as some say, of Juda. For those born and dwelling in some territory are called its children. [[2:1|that went out of the captivity|Qui ascenderunt de captivitate]], that is, from the land of their captivity, namely from Babylonia, [[2:1|which|quam]], that is, the people of which captivity, or which captive people, [[2:1|Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon|transtulerat Nabuchodonosor in Babylonem]], [[2:1|and who returned to Jerusalem and Juda|et reversi sunt in Jerusalem, et in Judam]], [[2:1|every man to his city|unusquisque in civitatem suam]], that is, to the places where the city of Jerusalem and the other towns of the kingdom of Juda had stood before they were destroyed by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:9||]]. For as birds love their nests and beasts their lairs, so men love their native places. Whence Laban said to Jacob: [[Gen 31:30|thou didst desire to go to thy friends, and hadst a longing after thy father's house|Ad tuos ire cupiebas, et desiderio tibi fuit domus patris tui]]. Hence the Apostle exhorts: [[Heb 10:25|Not forsaking our assembly|Non deserentes collectionem nostram]].

paras.t: Qui venerunt cum Zorobabel et ceteris qui exprimuntur in textu, videlicet, et cum Josue, Nehemia, Saraia, etc. Et iste Nehemias est alter ab eo, de quo infra habetur, et fuit dux populi postmodum.
paras.en: [[2:2|Who came with Zorobabel|Qui venerunt cum Zorobabel]] and the others who are named in the text, namely with [[2:2|Josue, Nehemia, Saraia|Josue, Nehemia, Saraia]], etc. And this Nehemias is another than the one of whom we read further on[[2 Esd 10:1||]][[2 Esd 12:26||]], who was afterwards leader of the people[[Ecclus 49:15||]].

paras.t: Numerus virorum populi Israel reversorum a Babylonis terra, est qui in littera subditur. Scriptura autem computat viros, qui scilicet ad minus viginti annorum exstiterant, potentes ad bella procedere. Filii Pharos ex tribu Juda, duo millia, etc. Planus est textus, nisi quod multa ponuntur hic nomina, quæ possunt esse nomina tam virorum seu patrumfamiliarum quam urbium; nec constat, qualiter potius sint sumenda. Nam et cives habitatoresque urbium, earum filii nuncupantur, sicut et ipsæ civitates vocantur filiæ regni sive provinciæ.
paras.en: [[2:2|The number of the men of the people of Israel|Numerus virorum populi Israel]] who returned from the land of Babylon is what follows in the text. Now Scripture counts the men, namely those who were at least twenty years old, able to go forth to war[[Num 1:3||]]. [[2:3|The children of Pharos|Filii Pharos]], of the tribe of Juda, [[2:3|two thousand|duo millia]], etc. The text is plain, except that many names are set down here which may be names either of men or fathers of families, or of cities; nor is it settled how they are rather to be taken. For the citizens and inhabitants of cities too are called their children, just as the cities themselves are called daughters of a kingdom or province.

paras.t: Consequenter inducitur numerus et genealogia sacerdotum. Sacerdotes, supple, fuerunt hi: Filii Jadaia in domo, hoc est familia, Josue, nongenti, etc. Levitæ, qui erant sacerdotibus inferiores ac subservientes, fuerunt: Filii Josue, etc. Cantores: Filii Asaph, qui fuit unus principalium cantorum, a David in tabernaculo Domini institutorum, ut primo libro Paralipomenon fertur: cujus posteri erant cantores; centum viginti octo, et unus eorum principalis fuit cantor. Qui psalmos David cantabant ac laudes divinas, potissime tempore sacrificiorum. Filii janitorum, hoc est custodum portarum templi seu atrii ejus. Nathinæi, qui erant (ut legitur) successores Gabaonitarum, portantes ligna et aquas ad locum cultus divini: quod officium imposuit eis Josue; filii servorum Salomonis, trecenti nonaginta duo. Omnes Israelitæ tempore Salomonis exsistentes, fuerunt servi ipsius; sed quoniam præcipua Salomonis occupatio exstitit circa templum, saltem ad tempus, ideo specialiter servi Salomonis vocantur, qui ad custodiam ac reparationem ædificiorum templi fuerunt ordinati.
paras.en: Next the number and genealogy of the priests is brought in. [[2:36|The priests|Sacerdotes]]: supply, were these: [[2:36|the children of Jadaia|Filii Jadaia]] [[2:36|of the house|in domo]], that is, family, [[2:36|of Josue, nine hundred|Josue, nongenti]], etc. [[2:40|The Levites|Levitæ]], who were below the priests and served them, were: [[2:40|the children of Josue|Filii Josue]], etc. [[2:41|The singing men: the children of Asaph|Cantores: Filii Asaph]], who was one of the chief singers appointed by David in the tabernacle of the Lord, as is told in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 16:5||]][[1 Par 25:2||]], whose descendants were singers: [[2:41|a hundred twenty-eight|centum viginti octo]], and one of them was the chief singer. They sang the psalms of David and the divine praises, above all at the time of the sacrifices. [[2:42|The children of the porters|Filii janitorum]], that is, of the keepers of the gates of the temple or of its court. [[2:43|The Nathinites|Nathinæi]], who were (as we read) the successors of the Gabaonites, carrying wood and water to the place of divine worship: which office Josue laid upon them[[Jos 9:27||]]; [[2:58|the children of the servants of Solomon, three hundred ninety-two|filii servorum Salomonis, trecenti nonaginta duo]]. All the Israelites living in Solomon's time were his servants; but since Solomon's chief occupation was about the temple, at least for a time, those are specially called servants of Solomon who were appointed to the keeping and repair of the buildings of the temple.

paras.t: Et hi qui ascenderunt, etc. Hic numerantur aliqui, qui certificare non poterant se esse de semine filiorum Israel: et quidam eorum utebantur sacerdotali officio, vel posse se uti putabant. Unde et de filiis sacerdotum dicuntur in littera. Et quæsierunt scripturam genealogiæ suæ, hoc est historiam fide dignam, in qua linea generationis eorum contineretur, et non invenerunt, et ejecti sunt de sacerdotio, id est, prohibiti sunt fungi sacerdotali officio, ad vitandum periculum seu discrimen: quoniam jussum fuit a Deo in Exodo atque Levitico, ne quis sacerdotali fungeretur officio, nisi de semine Aaron oriundus. Unde nec in novo Testamento permittitur quis celebrare Missam, nisi probare possit esse se ordinatum.
paras.en: [[2:59|And these are they that came up|Et hi qui ascenderunt]], etc. Here some are numbered who could not make certain that they were of the seed of the children of Israel; and some of them exercised the priestly office, or thought they could. Whence they are said in the text to be [[2:61|of the children of the priests|de filiis sacerdotum]]. [[2:62|These sought the writing of their genealogy|Et quæsierunt scripturam genealogiæ suæ]], that is, a trustworthy history in which the line of their descent was contained, [[2:62|and found it not, and they were cast out of the priesthood|et non invenerunt, et ejecti sunt de sacerdotio]], that is, they were forbidden to perform the priestly office, to avoid peril or hazard: because it was commanded by God in Exodus and Leviticus that no one should perform the priestly office unless he were sprung from the seed of Aaron[[Ex 29:9||]][[Lev 8:1||]][[Num 3:10||]][[Num 16:40||]]. Whence in the New Testament too no one is permitted to celebrate Mass unless he can prove that he has been ordained.

paras.t: Et dixit Athersatha eis, ut non comederent de sancto sanctorum, hoc est cibos præcipue sanctos, videlicet ad esum et usum sacerdotum solummodo deputatos, ut erant aliquæ partes hostiarum pro peccato pacificarumque oblationum, et panes propositionis, donec surgeret sacerdos doctus atque perfectus, id est tam eminenter eruditus, virtuosus, ac sapiens, quod Deus super re hac eum certificaret per revelationem, seu alio modo. Præterea Athersatha iste dicitur Nehemias fuisse: nam infra narratur Nehemias istud jussisse; atque, ut fertur, Athersatha interpretatur relaxatus, quoniam de consilio sapientium Hebræorum relaxatus fuit bibere vinum regis, cujus (ut infra habetur) fuit pincerna. Nam et Daniel describit, quod ipse Daniel et socii ejus rogaverunt eunuchum, ne cogerentur bibere de vino, unde bibebat rex, ne contaminarentur.
paras.en: [[2:63|And Athersatha said to them, that they should not eat of the holy of holies|Et dixit Athersatha eis, ut non comederent de sancto sanctorum]], that is, the foods especially holy, namely those set apart for the eating and use of the priests alone, such as certain parts of the victims for sin and of the peace offerings, and the loaves of proposition, [[2:63|till there arose a priest learned and perfect|donec surgeret sacerdos doctus atque perfectus]], that is, so eminently learned, virtuous and wise that God would make him certain about this matter by revelation or in some other way. Further, this Athersatha is said to have been Nehemias[[2 Esd 8:9||]]: for it is told further on that Nehemias commanded this[[2 Esd 7:65||]]; and, as is said, Athersatha means "released", because by the counsel of the wise men of the Hebrews he was released to drink the king's wine, whose cupbearer he was (as we read further on)[[2 Esd 1:11||]]. For Daniel too relates that he and his companions asked the eunuch that they might not be forced to drink of the wine the king drank, lest they be defiled[[Dan 1:8||]].

paras.t: Deinde ponitur summa prædictorum, et aliorum qui eis fuerant sociati. Nam et de aliis tribubus Israel quidam redierunt cum tribus tribubus jam præfatis. Nempe quando populus regni Juda captus est a Chaldæis, multi ex regno Israel in regno Juda commorabantur, qui manus evaserunt Assyriorum, et sub Ezechia rege converterunt se ad cultum Dei, et habitare cœperunt in terra Juda: et hi capti fuerunt cum populo Juda ab ipsis Chaldæis.
paras.en: Then the sum is given of those already named and of others who had joined them. For some of the other tribes of Israel also returned with the three tribes already mentioned. For when the people of the kingdom of Juda was taken captive by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:11||]], many of the kingdom of Israel were living in the kingdom of Juda, who had escaped the hands of the Assyrians, and under king Ezechias had turned to the worship of God[[2 Par 30:11||]][[2 Par 30:18||]] and begun to live in the land of Juda: and these were taken captive with the people of Juda by the Chaldeans.

3.title: Expositio capituli tertii: Jamque venerat mensis septimus
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: And now the seventh month was come

paras.t: Reparatio templi et altaris hic recitatur, qualiter scilicet sint incepta.
paras.en: Here the restoration of the temple and of the altar is related, namely how they were begun.

paras.t: Jamque venerat mensis septimus primi anni regressionis in Jerusalem: qui mensis dicitur correspondere nostro Septembri, et partim Octobri; et erant filii Israel in civitatibus suis. Congregatus est ergo omnis populus, a captivitate reversus, quasi vir unus, hoc est voluntate concordi, ad instaurandum altare ac templum: de quibus in Jeremia Dominus prædixit, Dabo eis cor unum et animam unam; in Jerusalem. Et surrexit Josue filius Josedec, et fratres ejus sacerdotes. Iste Josue, est Jesus filius Josedec, tunc pontifex Judæorum, ut Josephus refert undecimo libro Antiquitatum. De quo in Zacharia legitur: Audi, Jesu, sacerdos magne. Et Zorobabel filius Salathiel, et fratres ejus. Qui duo erant principales in isto negotio atque in populo illo.
paras.en: [[3:1|And now the seventh month was come|Jamque venerat mensis septimus]] of the first year of the return to Jerusalem: which month is said to correspond to our September, and partly to October; [[3:1|and the children of Israel were in their cities|et erant filii Israel in civitatibus suis]]. [[3:1|and the people gathered themselves together|Congregatus est ergo omnis populus]], returned from captivity, [[3:1|as one man|quasi vir unus]], that is, with one accord of will, to restore the altar and the temple: of whom the Lord foretold in Jeremias: [[Jer 32:39|I will give them one heart|Dabo eis cor unum]], and one soul [Jeremias has "and one way"; "one soul" recalls Acts 4:32]; [[3:1|to Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]]. [[3:2|And Josue the son of Josedec rose up, and his brethren the priests|Et surrexit Josue filius Josedec, et fratres ejus sacerdotes]]. This Josue is Jesus the son of Josedec, then high priest of the Jews, as Josephus relates in the eleventh book of the Antiquities. Of him we read in Zacharias: [[Zach 3:8|Hear, O Jesus thou high priest|Audi, Jesu, sacerdos magne]]. [[3:2|and Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and his brethren|Et Zorobabel filius Salathiel, et fratres ejus]]. These two were the chief men in this business and among that people.

paras.t: Et ædificaverunt altare Dei. Hoc fuit altare holocaustorum, in atrio factum sub dio, quia templum nondum fuit inceptum: et primo cœperunt altare construere, ut possent quotidie sacrificia immolare. Collocaverunt autem altare super bases suas, id est super convenientia fundamenta, deterrentibus eos per circuitum populis terrarum, id est gentilibus, et præsertim Samaritanis, quos in terra decem tribuum collocaverant reges Assyriorum: qui communiter fuerunt adversarii Judæorum; et obtulerunt super illud holocaustum Domino sacerdotes mane et vespere. Hoc fuit sacrificium juge et quotidianum, quo offerebatur quotidie agnus anniculus, id est unius anni, de mane, et item de vespere, sicut scriptum est in Numerorum libro, in quo Dominus ait: Hæc sunt sacrificia quæ offerre debetis: Agnos anniculos immaculatos duos quotidie in holocaustum sempiternum.
paras.en: [[3:2|and they built the altar of the God|et ædificaverunt altare Dei]]. This was the altar of holocausts, made in the court under the open sky, because the temple was not yet begun; and they began by building the altar first, so that they could offer sacrifices daily. [[3:3|And they set the altar of God upon its bases|Collocaverunt autem altare super bases suas]], that is, upon fitting foundations, [[3:3|while the people of the lands round about put them in fear|deterrentibus eos per circuitum populis terrarum]], that is, the gentiles, and especially the Samaritans, whom the kings of the Assyrians had settled in the land of the ten tribes[[4 Kings 17:24||]], who were commonly the adversaries of the Jews; [[3:3|and they offered upon it a holocaust to the Lord|et obtulerunt super illud holocaustum Domino]], the priests, [[3:3|morning and evening|mane et vespere]]. This was the continual, daily sacrifice, in which a lamb of a year, that is, one year old, was offered every day in the morning and again in the evening, as is written in the book of Numbers, where the Lord says: [[Num 28:3|These are the sacrifices which you shall offer: Two lambs of a year old without blemish every day for the perpetual holocaust:|Hæc sunt sacrificia quæ offerre debetis: Agnos anniculos immaculatos duos quotidie in holocaustum sempiternum]]

paras.t: Feceruntque solennitatem Tabernaculorum, sicut scriptum est in Levitico: quæ incepit quintadecima die septimi mensis, quia ibidem legitur: A quintodecimo die mensis hujus septimi erunt feriæ Tabernaculorum septem diebus. Qualiter autem illa solennitas celebrabatur, eodem capitulo et etiam infra in isto volumine continetur. Et holocaustum diebus singulis per ordinem secundum præceptum Dei, in Levitico et Numeris, ubi de his sacrificiis agitur, opus diei in die suo, id est sacrificium fiendum quolibet die præfixo. Et post hoc holocaustum juge, id est quotidianum, quod nullo die omittebatur propter quæcumque sacrificia alia immolanda, tam in calendis, id est neomeniis seu mensium exordiis, quam in universis solennitatibus Domini quæ erant consecratæ, id est in præcipuis festis legis, videlicet Paschæ, Pentecostes, Tubarum, Expiationis et Tabernaculorum: de quibus in Levitico et Numerorum libro ac Deuteronomio frequenter fit mentio; et in omnibus diebus, in quibus ultro offerebatur munus Domino, id est, sponte ex devotione ultra debitum fiebat a plebe oblatio.
paras.en: [[3:4|And they kept the feast of tabernacles, as it is written|Feceruntque solennitatem Tabernaculorum, sicut scriptum est]] in Leviticus: which began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, because we read there: [[Lev 23:34|From the fifteenth day of this same seventh month, shall be kept the feast of tabernacles, seven days|A quintodecimo die mensis hujus septimi erunt feriæ Tabernaculorum septem diebus]]. How that solemnity was celebrated is contained in the same chapter, and also further on in this volume. [[3:4|and offered the holocaust every day orderly according to the commandment|Et holocaustum diebus singulis per ordinem secundum præceptum]] of God in Leviticus and Numbers, where these sacrifices are treated[[Lev 23:36||]][[Num 28:1||]][[Num 29:1||]], [[3:4|the duty of the day in its day|opus diei in die suo]], that is, the sacrifice to be made on each appointed day. [[3:5|And afterwards the continual holocaust|Et post hoc holocaustum juge]], that is, the daily one, which was left out on no day for the sake of any other sacrifices to be offered, [[3:5|both on the new moons|tam in calendis]], that is, the neomenias or beginnings of the months, [[3:5|and on all the solemnities of the Lord, that were consecrated|quam in universis solennitatibus Domini quæ erant consecratæ]], that is, on the chief feasts of the law, namely of the Pasch, of Pentecost, of Trumpets, of Expiation and of Tabernacles, of which mention is often made in Leviticus, the book of Numbers and Deuteronomy[[Lev 23:1||]][[Deut 16:1||]]; [[3:5|and on all in which a freewill offering was made to the Lord|et in omnibus diebus, in quibus ultro offerebatur munus Domino]], that is, an offering was made by the people of their own accord, out of devotion, beyond what was due.

paras.t: A primo die mensis septimi cœperunt offerre holocaustum Domino. Tunc enim erexerunt altare, ante cujus erectionem non poterant immolare. Porro templum Dei nondum fundatum erat. Dederunt autem principales inter Judæos pecunias latomis, id est lapidum cæsoribus, et cæmentariis, qui cum cæmento muros seu parietes ex lapidibus construebant. Cibum quoque, videlicet blada, potum et oleum dabant Sidoniis Tyriisque, id est viris operariis de Sidone et Tyro, ut deferrent, id est apportarent, ligna cedrina de Libano monte, in quo crescunt, ad mare Joppe, id est usque ad ripam maris Mediterranei, juxta quam sita est urbs nomine Joppe antiqua: quæ a Japhet filio Noe perhibetur fundata, ubi est portus Mediterranei maris; juxta quod præceperat Cyrus rex Persarum, qui (Josepho teste) jussit de suo sumptus in omnibus fieri. Sic et tertio Regum libro legitur Salomon dedisse blada et oleum Hiram regi Tyri, quatenus servi ipsius adducerent pro constructione templi ligna cedrina et abiegna: secundum quod Paralipomenon libro secundo additur et de vino, quod dedit Hiram regi.
paras.en: [[3:6|From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer holocausts to the Lord|A primo die mensis septimi cœperunt offerre holocaustum Domino]]. For then they set up the altar, before the setting up of which they could not offer sacrifice. [[3:6|but the temple of God was not yet founded|Porro templum Dei nondum fundatum erat]]. [[3:7|And they gave|Dederunt autem]], the chief men among the Jews, [[3:7|money to hewers of stones|pecunias latomis]], that is, cutters of stone, [[3:7|and to masons|et cæmentariis]], who built walls or partitions of stone with mortar. [[3:7|and meat and drink, and oil|Cibum quoque, videlicet blada, potum et oleum]] (meat, that is, corn) they gave [[3:7|to the Sidonians and Tyrians|Sidoniis Tyriisque]], that is, to workmen from Sidon and Tyre, [[3:7|to bring|ut deferrent]], that is, carry, [[3:7|cedar trees from Libanus|ligna cedrina de Libano]], the mountain on which they grow, [[3:7|to the sea of Joppe|ad mare Joppe]], that is, as far as the shore of the Mediterranean sea, beside which stands the ancient city named Joppe, which is said to have been founded by Japheth the son of Noe, where there is a harbour of the Mediterranean sea; [[3:7|according to the orders which Cyrus king of the Persians had given|juxta quod præceperat Cyrus rex Persarum]], who (as Josephus testifies) ordered the costs in everything to be met from his own purse. So too we read in the third book of Kings that Solomon gave corn and oil to Hiram king of Tyre, so that his servants should bring cedar and fir wood for the building of the temple[[3 Kings 5:11||]]: to which the second book of Paralipomenon adds wine also, which he gave to king Hiram[[2 Par 2:10||]].

paras.t: Anno autem secundo adventus eorum a Babylone ad templum Dei, id est ad locum templi nondum tunc incepti, cœperunt ædificare templum Zorobabel et Josue, etc., et constituerunt Levitas a viginti annis et supra, id est, qui erant ad minus viginti annorum, ut urgerent opus Domini, id est, sollicitarent ædificium templi. In libro Numerorum legitur Dominus præcepisse numerari Levitas a tricesimo anno usque ad annum quinquagesimum, ad portandum et faciendum sibi injuncta. Alio loco Numerorum habetur: Hæc est lex Levitarum: A viginti quinque annis et supra, ingredientur ut ministrent in tabernaculo fœderis. Quomodo ergo licuit istis constituere Levitas a viginti annis? Ad quod dicendum videtur, quod isti Levitæ dicuntur positi ad sollicitandum structuram templi. Si autem faciebant cetera opera Levitarum, forsan ex dispensatione sic factum est, quia pauci erant adhuc.
paras.en: [[3:8|And in the second year of their coming|Anno autem secundo adventus eorum]] from Babylon [[3:8|to the temple of God|ad templum Dei]], that is, to the place of the temple, not yet then begun, Zorobabel and Josue, etc., [[3:8|began|cœperunt]] to build the temple, [[3:8|and they appointed Levites from twenty years old and upward|et constituerunt Levitas a viginti annis et supra]], that is, those who were at least twenty years old, [[3:8|to hasten forward the work of the Lord|ut urgerent opus Domini]], that is, to press on the building of the temple. In the book of Numbers we read that the Lord commanded the Levites to be numbered from the thirtieth year to the fiftieth, to carry and do what was laid on them[[Num 4:3||]]. In another place of Numbers we have: [[Num 8:24|This is the law of the Levites: From twenty-five years old and upwards, they shall go in to minister in the tabernacle of the covenant|Hæc est lex Levitarum: A viginti quinque annis et supra, ingredientur ut ministrent in tabernaculo fœderis]]. How then was it lawful for these men to appoint Levites from twenty years old? To this it seems it must be said that these Levites are said to have been set to press on the building of the temple. But if they did the other works of the Levites too, perhaps this was done by dispensation, because they were still few.

paras.t: Stetitque Josue pontifex, et filii ejus et fratres ejus, quasi vir unus, id est ordinate atque concorditer, ut instarent super eos qui faciebant opus in templo Dei, id est in loco templi, hoc est ad dirigendum operarios ipsos ad agendum viriliter.
paras.en: [[3:9|Then Josue|Stetitque Josue]] the high priest [[3:9|and his sons and his brethren|et filii ejus et fratres ejus]], [[3:9|as one man|quasi vir unus]], that is, in order and with one accord, [[3:9|stood to hasten them that did the work in the temple of God|ut instarent super eos qui faciebant opus in templo Dei]], that is, in the place of the temple: that is, to direct the workmen themselves to act manfully.

paras.t: Fundato igitur templo, steterunt sacerdotes in ornatu suo, id est sacerdotalibus vestimentis induti, cum tubis, quarum usus fuit in cultu et obsequio Dei, et in jubilæo, et dicebantur tubæ sacerdotales: de quibus Josue ait. Fuerunt quoque tubæ, quarum usus fuit in bellis, et aliæ tubæ ad populum convocandum, sicut in libro scribitur Numerorum. Et Levitæ filii Asaph in cymbalis, id est cum talibus musicis instrumentis, de quibus prædictum est, ut laudarent Deum per manum David regis Israel, id est, secundum ordinationem David regis laudarent Dominum, in psalmis a David compositis. Et concinebant in hymnis et confessione Domino, Quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus super Israel: id est, in psalmis et laudibus aliis ac spiritualibus canticis pariter cecinerunt, Omnipotenti gratias agendo de templi fundatione. Omnis quoque populus Israel ibi præsens, vociferabatur clamore magno in laudando Dominum, eo quod fundatum esset templum Domini.
paras.en: [[3:10|And when the masons laid the foundations of the temple|Fundato igitur templo]], [[3:10|the priests stood in their ornaments|steterunt sacerdotes in ornatu suo]], that is, clothed in priestly vestments, [[3:10|with trumpets|cum tubis]], which were used in the worship and service of God and in the jubilee, and were called the priests' trumpets, of which Josue speaks[[Jos 6:4||]]. There were also trumpets used in wars, and other trumpets for calling the people together, as is written in the book of Numbers[[Num 10:2||]]. [[3:10|and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals|Et Levitæ filii Asaph in cymbalis]], that is, with such musical instruments, of which we spoke before[[1 Par 16:5||]], [[3:10|to praise God by the hands of David king of Israel|ut laudarent Deum per manum David regis Israel]], that is, they praised the Lord according to the ordinance of king David, in the psalms composed by David. [[3:11|And they sung together hymns, and praise to the Lord: because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever towards Israel|Et concinebant in hymnis et confessione Domino, Quoniam bonus, quoniam in æternum misericordia ejus super Israel]]: that is, they sang together in psalms and other praises and spiritual canticles, giving thanks to the Almighty for the founding of the temple. [[3:11|And all the people shouted with a great shout|Omnis quoque populus Israel ibi præsens, vociferabatur clamore magno]], all the people of Israel there present, [[3:11|praising the Lord, because the foundations of the temple of the Lord were laid|in laudando Dominum, eo quod fundatum esset templum Domini]].

paras.t: Plurimi etiam de sacerdotibus et Levitis et principes patrum, id est præcipui inter patres, et seniores qui viderant templum prius a Salomone constructum, quum fundatum esset: non quod fuerint quando illud templum fundabatur, sed quum fundatum, id est firmiter collocatum esset, in suo vigore subsistens; et hoc templum, id est templi hujus secundi fundamenta; flebant voce magna, tum ex recordatione destructionis illius primi celeberrimi templi, tum quia templum istud secundum fundatum, videbatur parvi momenti respectu templi prioris, nec apparebat quod unquam pertingeret ad notabilem venustatem et gloriam comparatione templi prioris. Hinc per Aggeum Dominus ait constructoribus templi secundi: Quis in vobis est derelictus, qui vidit domum istam in gloria sua prima? et quid vos videtis hanc nunc? Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit in oculis vestris? Et ibi consequenter Dominus consolabatur eos, dicendo: Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ magis quam primæ. Quod, sicut ibi expositum est, impletum est per Christi præsentiam, oblationem, prædicationem, miraculosasque actiones in templo secundo.
paras.en: [[3:12|But many of the priests and the Levites, and the chief of the fathers|Plurimi etiam de sacerdotibus et Levitis et principes patrum]], that is, the foremost among the fathers, [[3:12|and the ancients that had seen the former temple|et seniores qui viderant templum prius]] built by Solomon, when it was founded: not that they were there when that temple was being founded, but when it was founded, that is, firmly set up and standing in its strength; [[3:12|when they had the foundation of this temple before their eyes|et hoc templum]], that is, the foundations of this second temple, [[3:12|wept with a loud voice|flebant voce magna]], both at the remembrance of the destruction of that first and most renowned temple, and because this second temple, now founded, seemed of little account in respect of the former temple, nor did it appear that it would ever attain to any notable beauty and glory in comparison with the former temple. Hence the Lord says by Aggeus to the builders of the second temple: [[Agg 2:4|Who is left among you, that saw this house in its first glory? and how do you see it now? is it not in comparison to that as nothing in your eyes?|Quis in vobis est derelictus, qui vidit domum istam in gloria sua prima? et quid vos videtis hanc nunc? Numquid non ita est, quasi non sit in oculis vestris?]] And there the Lord goes on to console them, saying: [[Agg 2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ magis quam primæ]]. Which, as was explained there, was fulfilled by the presence, offering, preaching and miraculous deeds of Christ in the second temple.

5.title: Explanatio capituli quinti: Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: Now Aggeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesied

paras.t: Hic agitur de resumptione ædificationis templi, et de appellatione propter hoc facta ad Darium regem.
paras.en: Here the resumption of the building of the temple is treated, and the appeal made on that account to king Darius.

paras.t: Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo, prophetantes ad Judæos qui erant in Judæa et Jerusalem, in nomine Dei Israel. Isti duo fuerunt in terra Babyloniæ nati, et inter duodecim minores computantur Prophetas. Unde in Scholastica fertur historia: Ascensuri ex Babylonia in Judæam, alios hortabantur Judæos ut secum ascenderent, sed paucos invenerunt qui assentirent eis. Propterea in exhortatione et apparatu tres annos compleverunt, et in tertio anno regni Cyri egressi sunt sub Zorobabel duce eorum et Jesu pontifice, exhortantibus eos Zacharia propheta et Aggæo juvene, sed nondum propheta. Denique, mortuo Cambyse et Dario imperante, hi duo Prophetæ admonuerunt ipsum Zorobabel atque pontificem et populum, ut rursus inciperent prosequi ædificium templi et civitatis, etiam nondum ad hoc licentia obtenta a Dario, prædicentes ex revelatione divina, quod prosperaretur opus in manu eorum, nec Darius impediret.
paras.en: [[5:1|Now Aggeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesied to the Jews that were in Judea and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel.|Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo, prophetantes ad Judæos qui erant in Judæa et Jerusalem, in nomine Dei Israel]] These two were born in the land of Babylonia, and are counted among the twelve minor Prophets. Hence it is related in the Scholastic History: When they were about to go up from Babylonia into Judea, they urged the other Jews to go up with them, but found few who would agree with them. Therefore they spent three years in exhorting and in making ready, and in the third year of the reign of Cyrus they went out under Zorobabel their leader and Jesus the high priest, Zacharias the prophet exhorting them, and Aggeus, a young man but not yet a prophet. At length, when Cambyses was dead and Darius reigned, these two Prophets admonished Zorobabel himself, and the high priest, and the people, to begin again to carry on the building of the temple and of the city, even though leave for it had not yet been obtained from Darius, foretelling by divine revelation that the work would prosper in their hands, and that Darius would not hinder it.

paras.t: Verumtamen, secundum Josephum, Zorobabel audita promotione Darii in regem, festinanter eum accessit, quia jamdudum habuit familiarem amicitiam secum, atque (ut legitur) ex instigatione ipsius Zorobabel Darius fecit votum Deo Israel, quod si fieret rex, reædificaret civitatem Jerusalem et templum in ea. Concessit itaque Darius ipsi Zorobabel largam licentiam instaurandi templum et urbem, et privilegia multa. Sed sicut Magister in historiis scribit, iste accessus Zorobabel ad Darium, fuit postquam resumpsit ædificationem, dum principes Darii habitantes trans flumen petierunt a Zorobabel, qua auctoritate prosequeretur ædificationem dudum prohibitam, sicut jam ex textu patebit.
paras.en: However, according to Josephus, Zorobabel, on hearing that Darius had been raised to the throne, went to him in haste, because he had long had a close friendship with him; and (as we read) at the prompting of Zorobabel himself Darius had made a vow to the God of Israel that, if he became king, he would rebuild the city of Jerusalem and the temple in it. So Darius granted Zorobabel ample leave to restore the temple and the city, and many privileges. But, as the Master [that is, Peter Comestor, the "Master of the Histories"] writes in the Histories, this going of Zorobabel to Darius was after he had taken up the building again, when the princes of Darius who dwelt beyond the river demanded of Zorobabel by what authority he was carrying on a building that had long been forbidden, as will now appear from the text.

paras.t: In ipso tempore venit ad eos, id est ad Zorobabel et Judæos, Thathanai, qui erat dux trans flumen Euphraten, et Stharbusanai et consiliarii eorum, et dixerunt: Quis dedit vobis consilium, ut domum hanc ædificaretis, et muros ejus, civitatis aut templi, instauraretis? Ad quod respondimus eis, quæ essent nomina hominum auctorum illius ædificationis, id est, qui essent principales in opere illo: quod scilicet Aggæus et Zacharias ex divina revelatione hoc insinuarent esse agendum, et quod Zorobabel dudum amicus Darii, esset exsecutor operis hujus.
paras.en: [[5:3|And at the same time came to them|In ipso tempore venit ad eos]], that is, to Zorobabel and the Jews, [[5:3|Thathanai, who was governor beyond the river|Thathanai, qui erat dux trans flumen]] Euphrates, [[5:3|and Stharbuzanai, and their counsellors|et Stharbusanai et consiliarii eorum]]: [[5:3|and said|et dixerunt]]: [[5:3|Who hath given you counsel to build this house, and to repair the walls thereof|Quis dedit vobis consilium, ut domum hanc ædificaretis, et muros ejus]], of the city or of the temple? [[5:4|In answer to which we gave them the names of the men who were the promoters of|Ad quod respondimus eis, quæ essent nomina hominum auctorum]] [[5:4|that building|illius ædificationis]], that is, who were the chief in that work: namely, that Aggeus and Zacharias made known by divine revelation that this was to be done, and that Zorobabel, long a friend of Darius, was the one carrying out this work.

paras.t: Oculus autem Dei eorum, id est respectus divinæ pietatis et confortationis, factus est super senes Judæorum, eos corroborans, ita quod non cessaverunt ab incepto, et non potuerunt principes præfati inhibere eos, quia Judæi de ipsorum inhibitione non curaverunt. Vel quamvis venerunt cum inhibendi proposito, Omnipotens tamen immutavit corda eorum, ita quod non prohibuerunt. Prima tamen expositio aptior reputatur. Nam subditur: Placuitque utrique parti, puta Judæis et Samaritis, ut res ad Darium referretur, id est, causa ista ad judicium Darii regis deportaretur, quia tunc erat monarcha in oriente; et tunc satisfacerent adversus accusationem illam, id est, Judæi ex determinatione Darii responderent ad accusationem eis objectam, quod incaute haberent se, ædificando sic sine licentia regis.
paras.en: [[5:5|But the eye of their God|Oculus autem Dei eorum]], that is, the regard of the divine goodness and strengthening, [[5:5|was upon the ancients of the Jews|factus est super senes Judæorum]], strengthening them, so that they did not cease from what they had begun, [[5:5|and they could not hinder them|et non potuerunt principes præfati inhibere eos]], that is, the aforesaid princes could not, because the Jews paid no heed to their forbidding. Or: although they came with the purpose of hindering them, the Almighty nevertheless changed their hearts, so that they did not forbid them. The first exposition, however, is thought the more fitting. For it is added: [[5:5|And it was agreed|Placuitque]] by both parties, namely the Jews and the Samaritans, [[5:5|that the matter should be referred to Darius|ut res ad Darium referretur]], that is, that this case should be carried to the judgment of king Darius, because he was then monarch in the East; [[5:5|and then they should give satisfaction concerning that accusation|et tunc satisfacerent adversus accusationem illam]], that is, that the Jews, by the decision of Darius, should answer the accusation laid against them, that they were behaving rashly in building thus without the king's leave.

paras.t: Exemplar epistolæ quam misit Thathanai ad Darium, id est, sermo epistolæ quam miserant ei hi, qui cum ipso Thathanai scripserunt Dario regi, cui scripserunt sic: Dario regi pax omnis, id est pax perfecta, seu pax interior, exterior, præsens et futura. Notum sit regi, isse, id est ivisse, nos ad Judæam ad domum Dei magni. Isti enim Samaritani cum diis suis colebant et Deum Israel, quem magnum et summum esse credebant. Quæ ædificatur lapide impolito, id est ex impolitis seu non sculptis lapidibus, et ligna ponuntur in parietibus; opusque illud diligenter exstruitur, crescitque in manibus eorum.
paras.en: [[5:6|The copy of the letter that Thathanai|Exemplar epistolæ quam misit Thathanai]] sent [[5:6|to Darius|ad Darium]], that is, [[5:7|The letter which they sent him|sermo epistolæ quam miserant ei]], those who wrote to king Darius together with Thathanai himself, to whom they wrote thus: [[5:7|To Darius the king all peace|Dario regi pax omnis]], that is, perfect peace, or peace within and without, present and to come. [[5:8|Be it known to the king, that we went|Notum sit regi, isse]], that is, *ivisse* [the fuller form of the same word, "to have gone"], [[5:8|to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God|nos ad Judæam ad domum Dei magni]]. For these Samaritans worshipped the God of Israel too, together with their own gods[[4 Kings 17:33||]][[4 Kings 17:41||]], and believed him to be great and supreme. [[5:8|which they are building with unpolished stones|Quæ ædificatur lapide impolito]], that is, of rough or uncarved stones, [[5:8|and timber is laid in the walls|et ligna ponuntur in parietibus]]: [[5:8|and this work is carried on diligently and advanceth in their hands|opusque illud diligenter exstruitur, crescitque in manibus eorum]].

paras.t: Interrogavimus ergo senes illos: Quis dedit vobis potestatem, ut domum hanc ædificaretis? Responderunt: Nos sumus servi Dei cæli et terræ, et ædificamus templum quod erat exstructum ante hos annos multos, id est, ædificamus templum simile templo olim a Salomone constructo.
paras.en: [[5:9|And we asked those ancients|Interrogavimus ergo senes illos]]: [[5:9|Who hath given you authority to build this house|Quis dedit vobis potestatem, ut domum hanc ædificaretis?]]? They answered: [[5:11|We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building a temple that was built these many years ago|Nos sumus servi Dei cæli et terræ, et ædificamus templum quod erat exstructum ante hos annos multos]], that is, we are building a temple like the temple built long ago by Solomon.

paras.t: Itaque ex eo tempore quo fundamenta templi sunt a Zorobabel seu Sassabasar posita usque nunc, ædificabatur templum, non continue, sed interveniente longa interruptione ex Cambysis prohibitione, ut patuit capitulo præcedente.
paras.en: And so [[5:16|from that time|ex eo tempore]] when the foundations of the temple were laid by Zorobabel, or Sassabasar, [[5:16|until now|usque nunc]] the temple was in building, not without a break, but with a long interruption coming between, through the prohibition of Cambyses, as was shown in the preceding chapter[[1 Esd 4:21||]][[1 Esd 4:24||]].

paras.t: Nunc ergo si videtur regi bonum, recenseat in bibliotheca regis, id est in armario seu repositorio librorum suorum annalium et historialium, quæ bibliotheca est in Babylone, id est in terra Babyloniæ: siquidem urbs Babylon fuit destructa; utrumnam a Cyro rege jussum sit ut ædificaretur domus Dei in Jerusalem, et voluntatem regis super hac re mittat ad nos.
paras.en: [[5:17|Now therefore if it seem good to the king, let him search in the king's library|Nunc ergo si videtur regi bonum, recenseat in bibliotheca regis]], that is, in the press or store-room of his books of annals and histories, [[5:17|which is in Babylon|quæ bibliotheca est in Babylone]], that is, in the land of Babylonia, since the city of Babylon had been destroyed; [[5:17|whether it hath been decreed by Cyrus the king, that the house of God in Jerusalem should be built|utrumnam a Cyro rege jussum sit ut ædificaretur domus Dei in Jerusalem]], [[5:17|and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter|et voluntatem regis super hac re mittat ad nos]].

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Tunc Darius rex præcepit, et recensuerunt in bibliotheca
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Then king Darius gave orders, and they searched in the library

paras.t: Præceptum Darii de templo ædificando et consummando, hic ponitur.
paras.en: Here is set down the command of Darius for the building and completing of the temple.

paras.t: Tunc Darius rex præcepit ministris et scriptoribus suis, et recensuerunt, id est inquisierunt, in bibliotheca librorum continentium gesta præcedentium regum, qui erant in Babylone, id est in regno Babylonis, prout se ante extenderat et includebat multa et magna regna; et inventum est in Ecbatanis, quod est castrum. In libro Judith habetur, quod Ecbatanis fuit potentissima civitas: quomodo ergo vocatur castrum? Forsan, quoniam instar fortalitii fuit firmissime facta, sicut secundum quorumdam expositionem Christus de Jerusalem dixit discipulis: Ite in castellum quod contra vos est. Vel forte Ecbatanis sumitur hic pro castro, non pro civitate. In Medena provincia, id est in regno Mediæ seu Medorum, inventum est ibi volumen unum, talisque in eo scriptus erat commentarius, id est tractatus expositorius rei gestæ per Cyrum.
paras.en: [[6:1|Then king Darius gave orders|Tunc Darius rex præcepit]] to his ministers and scribes, [[6:1|and they searched|et recensuerunt]], that is, made inquiry, [[6:1|in the library of the books|in bibliotheca librorum]] that contained the deeds of the former kings, [[6:1|that were laid up in Babylon|qui erant in Babylone]], that is, in the kingdom of Babylon, as it had formerly stretched out and taken in many great kingdoms; [[6:2|And there was found in Ecbatana, which is a castle|et inventum est in Ecbatanis, quod est castrum]]. In the book of Judith we read that Ecbatana was a most powerful city[[Jdt 1:1||]]: how then is it called a castle? Perhaps because it was made very strong, like a fortress; as, according to some men's explanation, Christ said to his disciples of Jerusalem: [[Matt 21:2|Go ye into the village that is over against you|Ite in castellum quod contra vos est]][[Mark 11:2||]] [*castellum*, literally "a castle" or "fortified place", where the Douay-Rheims has "village"]. Or perhaps Ecbatana is taken here for a castle, not for the city. [[6:2|in the province of Media|In Medena provincia]], that is, in the kingdom of Media or of the Medes, there was found [[6:2|a book|volumen unum]], [[6:2|in which this record was written|talisque in eo scriptus erat commentarius]], *record* [*commentarius*], that is, an expository account of what was done by Cyrus.

paras.t: Anno primo Cyri regis, Cyrus rex decrevit ut domus Dei quæ est, id est, esse debet, vel cujus locus est, in Jerusalem, ædificaretur in loco ubi immolent hostias, et ut ponant fundamenta supportantia altitudinem, id est structuram templi, quod erit in altitudine sexaginta cubitorum, et latitudinem cubitorum sexaginta. Aliqui opinantur, quod latitudo sumatur improprie hic pro longitudine templi, præsertim quum latitudo templi Salomonis non fuerit nisi cubitorum viginti. Verumtamen Josephus etiam refert sicut in textu habetur. Et ordines de lapidibus impolitis tres, et sic ordines de lignis novis. Hoc videtur ex verbis Josephi quasi exponi, dum ait: Et faciant tres parietes lapideos ipsius, videlicet templi, et unum parietem ligneum ex materiis ipsius provinciæ. Præterea objici potest, quia si templum istud secundum, fuit altitudinis sexaginta cubitorum, videtur fuisse altius templo Salomonis, quod habuit triginta cubitos in altitudine, prout tertio libro Regum habetur. Et respondendum, quod templum Salomonis fuit triginta cubitorum in altitudine usque ad primum tabulatum, deinde totidem usque ad tabulatum secundum, et ab illo usque ad verticem habuit adhuc in altitudine cubitos sexaginta. Unde tota ejus altitudo describitur secundo libro Paralipomenon ubi habetur: Porro altitudo centum viginti cubitorum erat.
paras.en: [[6:3|In the first year of Cyrus the king: Cyrus the king decreed, that the house of God|Anno primo Cyri regis, Cyrus rex decrevit ut domus Dei]] [[6:3|which is|quæ est]], that is, ought to be, or whose place is, [[6:3|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], [[6:3|should be built|ædificaretur]] [[6:3|in the place where they may offer sacrifices|in loco ubi immolent hostias]], [[6:3|and that they lay the foundations that may support the height|et ut ponant fundamenta supportantia altitudinem]], that is, the structure of the temple, which will be [[6:3|the height of threescore cubits|sexaginta cubitorum]], [[6:3|and the breadth of threescore cubits|et latitudinem cubitorum sexaginta]]. Some think that *breadth* is taken here improperly for the length of the temple, especially since the breadth of Solomon's temple was only twenty cubits[[3 Kings 6:2||]]. Yet Josephus too reports it as it stands in the text. [[6:4|Three rows of unpolished stones, and so rows of new timber|ordines de lapidibus impolitis tres, et sic ordines de lignis novis]]. This seems to be as it were explained by the words of Josephus, where he says: And let them make three walls of it, namely of the temple, of stone, and one wall of wood from the timber of that province. Further, it can be objected that if this second temple was sixty cubits high, it seems to have been higher than Solomon's temple, which was thirty cubits in height, as we have in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 6:2||]]. And the answer is that Solomon's temple was thirty cubits high up to the first storey, then as many again up to the second storey, and from that to the top it had sixty cubits more in height. Whence its whole height is described in the second book of Paralipomenon, where we have: [[2 Par 3:4|the height was a hundred and twenty cubits|Porro altitudo centum viginti cubitorum erat]].

paras.t: Nunc ergo, Thathanai et qui estis trans fluvium, procul recedite ab illis, scilicet Judæis reædificantibus templum et urbem Jerusalem, et dimittite fieri templum Dei a duce Judæorum. Et offerant oblationes Deo cæli, orentque pro vita regis Darii et filiorum ejus prospere conservanda. Circa hoc scribit quidam: Ex hoc patet, quod rex iste habebat fidem unius veri Dei. Verumtamen, an habuit fidem formatam vel solum informem, an potius solummodo fidem suasam et quamdam credulitatem fidei similem, non autem fidem quæ est theologica virtus, puto incertum. Nam (ut patuit) etiam Samaritani idololatræ, credebant, supplicabant et sacrificabant uni vero Deo. Similiter Assuerus, cujus conjux fuit Esther, credebat esse unum verum et summum Deum, omnium provisorem, ut patet in ejus epistolis, præsertim Esther ultimo. Et tamen isti non habuerunt fidem quæ est virtus theologica, nec formatam neque informem, sicut neque hæretici nec Sarraceni, qui unum Deum, non idola colunt.
paras.en: [[6:6|Now therefore Thathanai|Nunc ergo, Thathanai]], [[6:6|who are beyond the river, depart far from them|et qui estis trans fluvium, procul recedite ab illis]], that is, from the Jews who are rebuilding the temple and the city of Jerusalem, [[6:7|And let that temple of God be built by the governor of the Jews|et dimittite fieri templum Dei a duce Judæorum]]. [[6:10|And let them offer oblations to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king|Et offerant oblationes Deo cæli, orentque pro vita regis]] Darius, [[6:10|and of his children|et filiorum ejus]], that it may be prosperously preserved. On this a certain writer says: From this it is plain that this king had faith in the one true God. Yet whether he had formed faith or only unformed faith, or rather only a persuaded faith and a certain credulity like faith, but not the faith which is a theological virtue, I think is uncertain [formed faith is faith quickened by charity; unformed faith is true faith without charity]. For (as was shown) even the idolatrous Samaritans believed in, prayed to and sacrificed to the one true God[[4 Kings 17:33||]]. Likewise Assuerus, whose wife was Esther, believed that there is one true and supreme God, who provides for all, as is plain in his letters, especially in the last chapter of Esther[[Esth 16:16||]]. And yet these men did not have the faith which is a theological virtue, neither formed nor unformed, just as neither heretics nor Saracens have it, who worship one God and not idols.

paras.t: A me ergo Dario rege positum est decretum, id est ordinatio et præceptum, ut omnis homo qui hanc mutaverit jussionem, id est, transgressus fuerit eam, tollatur lignum de domo ipsius, si habuerit domum et lignum pro patibulo aptum: alioqui aliunde sumatur hujusmodi lignum: et configatur in eo. Domus autem ejus publicetur, id est, facultates ipsius ad fiscum pertineant regis. Deus qui habitare facit nomen suum ibi, id est, qui in templo Jerusalem jussit se invocari, nominari, laudari, et qui se ipsum voluit ibi per specialem gratiam esse et habitare, dissipet omnia regna, et populum qui extenderit manum suam ut repugnet, et dissipet domum Dei.
