paras.en: [[6:11|And I have made a decree|A me ergo Dario rege positum est decretum]], by me, king Darius, that is, an ordinance and command: [[6:11|That if any whosoever, shall alter this commandment|ut omnis homo qui hanc mutaverit jussionem]], that is, transgress it, [[6:11|a beam be taken from his house|tollatur lignum de domo ipsius]], if he has a house and a beam fit for a gibbet; otherwise let such a beam be taken from elsewhere: [[6:11|and he be nailed upon it|et configatur in eo]]. [[6:11|and his house be confiscated|Domus autem ejus publicetur]], that is, let his goods belong to the king's treasury. [[6:12|And may the God, that hath caused his name to dwell there|Deus qui habitare facit nomen suum ibi]], that is, who commanded that he be called upon, named and praised in the temple of Jerusalem, and who willed himself to be and to dwell there by special grace, [[6:12|destroy all kingdoms, and the people that shall put out their hand to resist, and to destroy the house of God|dissipet omnia regna, et populum qui extenderit manum suam ut repugnet, et dissipet domum Dei]].

paras.t: Ædificaverunt Judæi templum et urbem, jubente Deo per Aggeum et Zachariam prophetas, et jubente Cyro et Dario et Artaxerxe regibus Persarum; et compleverunt domum Dei. Ex qua forma verborum patet falsitas Rabbi Salomonis, dicentis quod Artaxerxes iste fuit idem qui Darius: quod si verum esset, Scriptura non loqueretur de eo et Dario cum interpositione hujusmodi conjunctionis copulativæ. Idcirco cum Josepho dicendum, quod Artaxerxes ille fuit filius Darii, et a Josepho Xerxes vocatur. Nec obstat, quod templum dicitur esse completum sexto Darii anno, videlicet quoad ædificium ejus secundum se: multa tamen deerant ejus ornatui et utensilibus et ædibus in gyro fiendis pro templi ministris. Usque ad diem tertium mensis Adar, qui duodecimus mensis est apud Judæos.
paras.en: The Jews built the temple and the city[[6:14||]], [[6:14|by the commandment of the God of Israel|jubente Deo]] through the prophets Aggeus and Zacharias[[Agg 1:1||]][[Zach 1:1||]][[Zach 4:9||]], [[6:14|and by the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes kings of the Persians|et jubente Cyro et Dario et Artaxerxe regibus Persarum]][[1 Esd 1:3||]][[2 Esd 2:8||]]; [[6:15|And they were finishing this house of God|et compleverunt domum Dei]]. From this form of words the falsity of Rabbi Solomon is plain, who says that this Artaxerxes was the same as Darius: for if that were true, Scripture would not speak of him and of Darius with such a copulative conjunction set between them. Therefore it must be said with Josephus that that Artaxerxes was the son of Darius, and is called Xerxes by Josephus. Nor is it any objection that the temple is said to have been completed in the sixth year of Darius, namely as to its building in itself: yet much was still lacking to its adornment and furnishings and to the dwellings to be made round about it for the ministers of the temple. [[6:15|until the third day of the month of Adar|Usque ad diem tertium mensis Adar]], which is the twelfth month among the Jews.

paras.t: Deinde in littera describitur, qualiter Judæi seu filii transmigrationis, id est de transmigratione et captivitate reversi, fecerunt dedicationem templi; et pontifex ac majores fecerunt sacerdotes ac Levitas stare ordinate secundum congruentiam officiorum suorum in vicibus suis, in quibus ministrare debebant et exercere opera Dei, sacrificando, laudando, et circa hostias præparandas ministerium exhibendo, sicut scriptum est in libro Moysis, præsertim in Levitico et libro Numerorum per diversa capitula: et plana est littera.
paras.en: Then the text describes how the Jews, or [[6:16|the children of the captivity|filii transmigrationis]], that is, those returned from the transmigration and captivity, [[6:16|kept the dedication|fecerunt dedicationem]] of the temple; and the high priest and the elders made the priests and Levites stand in order, according to the fitness of their offices, [[6:18|in their courses|in vicibus suis]], in which they were to minister and to do [[6:18|the works of God|opera Dei]], by sacrificing, by praising, and by serving about the preparing of the victims, [[6:18|as it is written in the book of Moses|sicut scriptum est in libro Moysis]], especially in Leviticus and in the book of Numbers, in various chapters: and the text is plain.

paras.t: Et purificati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ, id est, ad faciendum pascha secundum legem erant dispositi et purgati per orationes, lotiones et continentiam, atque per immunitatem ab irregularitatibus et immunditiis legis, a quibus debebant esse immunes aut purgati pascha facturi et agnum paschalem manducaturi: de quibus omnibus in Exodo, Levitico et ceteris Moysis libris diffuse tractatur. Purificati sunt ergo quasi vir unus, id est omnes concorditer sine exceptione. Et fecerunt solennitatem Azymorum septem diebus in lætitia, quoniam lætificaverat eos Dominus, gratiose agendo cum ipsis, et converterat cor regis Assur ad eos, ut adjuvaret manus eorum, id est, mentem Darii regis inclinaverat ad faciendum tam liberaliter et benigne cum ipsis, et ad habendum se tam devote circa Deum et templum. Dicitur autem Darius rex Persarum, rex Assur, quia et regnum Assyriorum fuit sub ejus imperio.
paras.en: [[6:20|For all the priests and the Levites were purified|Et purificati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ]], that is, to keep the pasch according to the law they were prepared and cleansed by prayers, washings and continence, and by freedom from the irregularities and uncleannesses of the law, from which those who were to keep the pasch and eat the paschal lamb had to be free or cleansed: of all which Exodus, Leviticus and the other books of Moses treat at length. So they were purified [[6:20|as one man|quasi vir unus]], that is, all with one accord, without exception. [[6:22|And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy, for the Lord had made them joyful|Et fecerunt solennitatem Azymorum septem diebus in lætitia, quoniam lætificaverat eos Dominus]], dealing graciously with them, [[6:22|and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, that he should help their hands|et converterat cor regis Assur ad eos, ut adjuvaret manus eorum]], that is, he had inclined the mind of king Darius to deal so freely and kindly with them, and to bear himself so devoutly towards God and the temple. And Darius, king of the Persians, is called king of Assyria because the kingdom of the Assyrians too was under his rule.
